# Metadata
![](images/metadata_2.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

As with most analysis we require metadata. 
Our metadata table requires:

- Columns of the different metadata variables
    - The column names are the names of the variables
- Rows of observations per sample
    - The row names need to contain the same sample names as the [count table](/relative/count_table.qmd)

## Extract metadata

Extract and check our metadata.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Extract metadata from phyloseq as data.frame
metadf <- genus_pseq |> 
    microbiome::meta()
#Check rows 1:5
metadf |> dplyr::slice(1:5)
```

Capitalise columns we'll use as fixed effects. 
This is to make the MaAsLin3 output look nicer.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
#Capitalise column names for MaAsLin3 output
metadf <- metadf |>
    dplyr::rename(Site=site, Media=media)
```

## Fixed effects and random effects
<center>
![](images/dice_three.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}
</center>

There are three main types of metadata variables for `MaAsLin3`. 
These are:

- __Categorical fixed effects__
    - A categorical variable that is related to your hypothesis and requires evaluation
    - These need to be factors in your metadata 
        - The first level is the reference group
        - All other levels are compared to the reference in pairwise fashion (i.e. the query)
        - For example healthy vs disease states
    - We will use `Site` and `Media` as categorical fixed effects
- __Continuous fixed effects__
    - This could be a continuous variable that is related to your hypothesis and requires evaluation (e.g. dosage)
    - Or it could be a continuous control variable (e.g. age)
    - We will use `Reads` (read counts/depth) as a continuous control variable (see the [read counts page](/maaslin3/read_counts.qmd))
- __Random effects__
    - Categorical variables to include that you are not necessarily interested in evaluating
    - These don't need to be factors since a reference group is not required
    - An example includes experimental blocks, different sequencing runs, or subjects
    - We won't use any random effects in our analysis

More theory and considerations are included in the later pages:

- [Fixed effects](/maaslin3/fixed_effects.qmd)
- [Random effects](/maaslin3/random_effects.qmd)

## Factorisation
![](images/factor_key.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

We are going to use `Site` and `Media` as categorical fixed effects.
Therefore, we need to set the  order of their factor levels.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Factors"}
A factor is R’s way of storing categorical data. 
It tells the model to compare categories, and lets us set which category is used as the reference level.

For more info please see: [R primer for omics explanation of factors](https://cgr-liverpool.github.io/R_primer_f81b92/course/14-Plots_scatterplot_and_box_plots.html#factors)
:::

Before factor ordering, let's see what groupings are in the two variables.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Check unique values of site and media
metadf |> dplyr::pull(site) |> unique()
metadf |> dplyr::pull(media) |> unique()
```

We have 3 for `Site`.
Let's use `UD` as the reference group and `MD` and `LD` as the queries.
We've chosen `UD` as it is the site with the lowest anthropisation.

We have four groups for `Media`.
We'll use `ENV` as the reference so all media groups are compared to it.

Type and run the below code to order tje factor levels of the two metadata variables.
The code uses some piping and the [`dplyr::mutate()` function](https://cgr-liverpool.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/mutate.html).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Factorise to order our categorical fixed effects
metadf <- metadf |>
    #Factorise site with UD as the reference level
    dplyr::mutate(site=factor(site,
                              levels = c("UD","MD","LD"))) |>
    #Factorise media with ENV as the reference level
    dplyr::mutate(media=factor(media,
                               levels = c("ENV","CVP","KBC","TSA")))
```


::: {.callout-note}
For the purposes of setting a reference it only matters which group is set as the first group.
The order of the subsequent levels does not matter for the MaAsLin3 analysis we will carry out.
:::

Great! Next we'll add read counts/depth to the metadata table.
